quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of these
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating before or while you drink slows alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly turn the wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and gradually steer back onto the road.
Brake hard and stop.
Gently brake and slowly turn the wheel to return to the road safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly turn the wheel to return to the road safely.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slowly reduce speed by gently braking. At a safe speed, turn the wheel to return to the road. Do not sharply turn the wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.
A hill is coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: When must pedestrians yield to motor vehicles?

options.text: When crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection.
When crossing in a marked crosswalk.
When the vehicle is a pickup truck.
Only in city limits.

questions.correctAnswerText: When crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians must yield to vehicles when crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection. They must also yield when a traffic signal tells them to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead has one-way traffic only.
Only one car can use the bridge at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns drivers that an upcoming bridge may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck. You should be careful.

questions.question: An oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle is coming at you head-on in your lane, honk to get their attention. If they don't move, steer to the right. Steering left is dangerous because the other driver may correct at the last moment and you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily to reduce the impact.

questions.question: A flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone. What must you do?

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says something else.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow the normal traffic rules as if there were no construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a flagger directs you. Not following a flagger's directions is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. You must immediately move to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels left.
Turn your wheels right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a parking space, checking traffic, and signaling, stop parallel to the vehicle directly ahead of your parking space before turning your wheel to park.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop ahead.
Buggy warning.
Limited parking.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and prepare drivers for upcoming road hazards. This sign tells drivers that a stop sign is coming and they should be ready to stop before going on.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. Use your turn signal when slowing down, stopping, or changing direction. Use your emergency lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the space between your vehicle and the car ahead. Your vehicle needs more time to stop in these conditions.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?

options.text: In curves and on hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers to defend yourself in traffic.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. This helps you avoid problems with reckless, careless, or drunk drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers about railroad crossings. You must yield to trains and never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What is the minimum safe following distance between vehicles?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
200 feet.
300 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a three-second distance between your vehicle and the car ahead. At high speeds or in bad weather, increase this distance.

questions.question: When stopped at a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again in case you missed any vehicles.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal to signal your intentions.
Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.
Use your cell phone to contact the police to determine if the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to contact the police to determine if the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and use your turn signal. Look for other drivers doing the same. Never use your phone while driving to check road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so badly that they seem drunk. Opening a window, playing loud music, or drinking coffee does not make them truly alert.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass more easily and quickly.

questions.question: When a driver is tailgating you:

options.text: Move right if there is an open lane.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear. Then slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If tailgated, move right if possible. If you cannot move right, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slow down gradually. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: After the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when signals warn of a train. These signals include red flashing lights, lowered gates, flaggers, or train sounds. Do not go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: You may continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
Pedestrians are crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, you should:

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and apply steady brake pressure.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and apply steady brake pressure.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure to the brake. Pull off the road when safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for vehicles and pedestrians to clear before proceeding.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Stopping too much.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. If you drive too fast, your tires lose grip and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A volunteer group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the roadway ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: When may you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering any intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs mean:

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other drivers.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other drivers.
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangular sign means yield. Let other traffic pass, then proceed when the road is clear and safe.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions hurt your driving. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress makes it hard to concentrate on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to drive when you feel emotionally upset.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:

options.text: Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.
Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
Help cure your illness.
Improve your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs makes both stronger. It is unsafe to drive after alcohol or drugs alone. Mixing them together is even more dangerous.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal a lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you stay safe.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:

options.text: Have to stop quickly.
Are passing another car.
Have lost control of your car.
Are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This warns other drivers of danger.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.
The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.
The car in which the driver sounds his horn first has the right-of-way.
The car that is traveling the fastest has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, yield to any vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.
Continue driving when you think most kids are done exiting the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: When a school bus shows its stop arm, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm goes down.

questions.question: A green arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed, but only if there is also a circular green light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. You must turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal before merging. Match the speed of traffic and yield to other vehicles. This helps you merge safely.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger. Slow down and be careful.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, you should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light.
